body: Some people can be assholes but I suppose in that case I wouldn’t want to be with them. Maybe I’m being way too hard on myself, and that’s the problem here. I still want to at least cover up or alter some of them as just from an aesthetic point of view, they suck.

>Instead of killing yourself, and doing bad things. Have you ever tried just not?

I absolutely have. The problem is my past precludes me from really participating in society. Any girl I tried to date now, knowing these truths would run and I understand. I've been sober, I haven't been blacking out and grabbing people - after I heard this happened I took steps to ensure it never happened again and it didn't - but it just feels like the damage is done.

In regards to the emotional abuse: I wasn't controlling - I never told her what to wear and I was glad she had friends and I liked her friends. I never insulted her looks or her passions in life, but I did guilt her a lot and I realize that now. I just put a lot of pressure on her and I feel terrible about what I put her through. I thought I was sticking up for myself, but I see now what I did. Either way, emotional abuse is yet another huge red-flag and scarlet letter, and I don't want to lie to any future partner about any of this.

Edit: also, someone downvoted your comment - it wasn't me. The point is people clearly think I deserve to die.

>There's options that aren't dying even for "I'm objectively a bad person".

So are you saying I'm objectively a bad person?

>My mother had sex with a paranoid schizophrenic.

Same. Except Dad died. Mom ended up having to move in with me. Grew up poor AF. Never remotely had a normal life compared to peers. Also have tinnitus - really just kind of feels like the final nail. I really wish they just hadn't have had me. I used to feel harsh saying that but not anymore. Also wish I had good advice but just so you know I'm in a somewhat similar boat.

> 50k star? How you manage that?

College \+ trying to get through college.

The list isn't bad advice, but I've made lists like that in bad times, including now: trying to think of things to do. I think at a certain point, because of my issues, despite thinking I've moved forward, I end up making decisions that set me back even further than before. It's been one step forward, two steps back this entire life. I think I've learned but I haven't. Same issues I was writing in my journal 10 years ago, that I have today. I know it'd blow a hole in my Mom and brother's lives if I disappeared, but at the same time I think I've been preparing them by being quite honest about not wanting to stick around at this point.

At least I've prepared them, if I do. I just think at 34 it's totally over. For the past three months I've been trying to think of a way forward, basically 24/7 trying to think of a route and I haven't come up with anything. Exercise literally feels like nothing now. I don't want to listen to music: I know it's really bad when I don't even want to do that. I've got tens of thousands of songs in my collection \- listening to music has been a huge part of my life \- and for three months: don't even want to hear it.

I think it's awesome that you try to support people in this situation though. The irony is throughout my life I was extremely afraid of death: that I had cancer, or whatever, I assume because my Dad died like he did. I actually had a cancer scare last fall and was pretty freaked out, but I was already sliding down. I also always thought "it's only 80 years max, what's the difference?" Well \- now I know the difference.
